text:
Alex Chen: Observed a 30-40% P99 latency regression on qwen-13B after the kernel-selector change from this morning. Rolling back the selector to the prev commit drops P99 back to baseline.
Priya Patel: Ugh. Do you have a profiler trace? rough numbers are fine.
Alex Chen: Pasted quick profile from a 1k seq run (single-worker warm):
```
wall_total: 1120ms
model_forward: 980ms
  attention_kernels: 420ms  (used: fused_fmha_opt)
  kv_read/write: 130ms
  kv_cache_miss_penalty: 60ms
  other: 370ms
p99_latency: 420ms (was ~300ms before selector change)
kv_cache_hit_rate: 96%
acceptance_rate(speculative): 0.72
rope_scale: 1.15 (Qwen uses base 10000 rot scaling vs 10000? confirm)
```
Alex Chen: Command to repro locally: `./run_profiler --model qwen-13b --seq 1024 --warm 50 --iters 200 --selector v2`
Marco Ruiz: Two quick hypotheses: 1) selector picked the Mistral-tailored fused path that assumes different RoPE packing, causing extra memory copies / misaligned loads. 2) speculative pairing left draft-model mismatched tokenizer or kv layout forcing decode fallback and extra remap costs.
Priya Patel: Can you dump the kernel metadata for the run? `--dump-kernel-backtrace` shows which kernels were chosen per layer. Also try forcing kernel `fused_fmha_qwen` if available.
Alex Chen: Dump attached (paste below):
```
layer 0: kernel=fused_fmha_opt (selected by selector v2)
layer 1: kernel=fused_fmha_opt
layer 2: kernel=fallback_attention (vector_remap)
...
last layers: kernel=fused_fmha_opt + remap stager
```
Tasha Nguyen: If we see remap stages, that's the expensive bit. Remap happens when kv layout or rotary base mismatches. Qwen's tokenizers historically need a slightly different RoPE interp. Could be a handshake problem when pairing draft models from a different family.
Priya Patel: Check the draft pairing config: I remember someone enabled family-agnostic pairing in the canary. That will let Mistral-like drafts attach to Qwen primaries and may trigger remap at accept time.
Alex Chen: Config snippet from runtime: `draft_pairing: { enable_family_agnostic: true, acceptance_threshold: 0.65 }`
Marco Ruiz: Step to reproduce: run a mixed-family speculative run with primary=qwen-13b and draft=mistral-7b (tokenizer mismatch on purpose). Monitor `kv_remap_ms` metric. If > ~20ms per token it's the remap.
Priya Patel: Quick mitigation: roll back family-agnostic pairing, or ensure kernel_selector prefers qwen-specific fused kernels when primary is Qwen. Also lower speculative acceptance threshold to cut wasted decodes (e.g., 0.5 -> 0.4).
perf-bot: deploy v2026.03.17-selector-v2 triggered at 2026-03-17T09:22:12Z by ci-bot. Canary ramp 100->20% now.
Tasha Nguyen: For a medium-term fix we should: 1) add kernel metadata checks to selector (model_family + rope_base + kv_layout) 2) add a fast path for no-remap when primary==draft_family 3) add runtime metric `kv_remap_count` and an alert when > 0.1% of requests.
Priya Patel: I can add a quick gating test in the selector unit tests to assert kernel compatibility matrix for Qwen.
Alex Chen: Action items: @Priya add selector unit test and temp rollback gate; @Marco add a canary that forces `fused_fmha_qwen`; @Tasha add `kv_remap_count` metric + dashboard tile. I'll hold off rolling back selector until we have the gating test in place (or we can rollback if heat increases).
Tasha Nguyen: Also we should tune the acceptance_rate for speculative decoding for qwen workloads — lower acceptance reduces wasted KV writes. Start with 0.4 for 24h and compare cost/latency.
Marco Ruiz: One more datapoint — I saw a small increase in memory allocations in the host trace when remap ran (heap churn spikes). That could amplify latency variance at p99.
Alex Chen: I'll run a 4-hour canary with family-agnostic=false and selector=v2 pinned-to-qwen-kernels. Posting results in ~3h.
Priya Patel: Thanks. If anyone hits the canary logs, search for `KV_REMAPPED` or `remap_stager` tags.
perf-bot: note: scheduled rollback window 2026-03-18T03:00Z if canary degrades >5% p99 for 30min.
Tasha Nguyen: Nice. Keep updates short here so oncall can follow. :thumbsup:
Alex Chen: Will update with canary numbers.
